subtopicTitle: Orbital elements (Keplerian) — semi-major axis a, eccentricity e, inclination i, RAAN Ω, argument of perigee ω, true anomaly ν

cards.front: Define the semi-major axis $a$ for an elliptical Keplerian orbit.
cards.back: Half the length of the major axis; it determines specific orbital energy via $\varepsilon = -\mu/(2a)$.

cards.front: What does eccentricity $e=0$ imply for the orbit shape?

cards.back: Angle between the orbital plane and the reference (e.g. equatorial) plane, $0^\circ \le i \le 180^\circ$.

cards.front: Define Right Ascension of the Ascending Node (RAAN) $\Omega$.
cards.back: Angle in the reference plane from the vernal equinox to the ascending node.
Angle in the orbital plane from the ascending node to the perigee direction.

cards.front: Write the polar equation for radial distance $r$ using $a$, $e$ and true anomaly $\nu$.
What does true anomaly $\nu$ represent geometrically?
cards.back: Angle at the focus between the perigee vector and the current position vector.
